surfaceForm: under documented institutional governance ... operationally bounded by the TAC's declared scope (TAC definition)
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch02-conceptual-frame-EN.tex | Sec 2.1 The Trusted Activity Context concept (\paragraph{Definition.})
proposedGenericDecision: Keep role-based 'institutional governance' phrasing; it is already generic. No governing-body name (rectorate/board) is asserted here.
rationale: The definition already speaks in role-based, institution-agnostic terms ('institutional governance', 'the institution'). No UL-specific shape leaks. Recorded as a deliberate keep so reviewers do not flag it.

surfaceForm: This re-frames several recurring difficulties in academic IT --- the researcher who is also a teacher, the visiting collaborator who is also a host, the administrative process that touches research data
proposedGenericDecision: Generic to any research-intensive institution; examples are role-based, not UL-bound. Retain.
rationale: 'academic IT' and the multi-hat examples are universally applicable across universities; no jurisdiction or named institution. Safe to keep.

surfaceForm: without surrendering control of the institutional perimeter ... do not compromise the institutional core or other contexts (Four founding principles: Trustworthiness, Dependability)
proposedGenericDecision: 'Institutional perimeter' / 'institutional core' assume a single bounded estate. For multi-campus or federated-college institutions this is a simplification but the language is still role-based. Generalize wording to 'institutional perimeter(s)' / 'institutional trust core' only if a federated/multi-site profile is in scope.
rationale: Implicitly assumes a single perimeter/core, which does not hold for federated or multi-campus institutions (e.g., Cambridge colleges). Low-severity: the phrasing is already abstract; flagged so a federated profile can soften it.

surfaceForm: A mature institution combines a relatively stable network segmentation (zones ...) with multiple dynamic TACs that operate within those zones ... network attachment appropriate to the activity's zone (research, teaching, administration, sensitive)
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch02-conceptual-frame-EN.tex | Sec 2.1 (\paragraph{Relation to segmentation.}) and itemized 'network attachment' bullet
proposedGenericDecision: The fixed zone taxonomy (research/teaching/administration/sensitive) is a design choice that some institutions name differently or extend (BYOD, IoT, Science DMZ per domain rules). Parameterize the zone label set rather than hard-code four names.
rationale: Zone names are conventional, not universal; the domain rules list a wider set (admin, research, teaching, BYOD, IoT, sensitive, Science DMZ). Parameterizing keeps the example illustrative without asserting a fixed institutional segmentation.

surfaceForm: The endpoint operating systems encountered at a typical research-intensive institution ... where present in the research-computing footprint
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch02-conceptual-frame-EN.tex | Sec 2.3 Endpoint OS integration matrix (intro paragraph and \paragraph{Other platforms.})
proposedGenericDecision: 'research-intensive institution' is a profile assumption that may not fit teaching-led or administrative institutions. Already hedged with 'typical'; keep but note as a scoping assumption that a non-research profile would adjust.
rationale: Role-based and already qualified as 'typical'. Not UL-specific. Flagged at low confidence only because the research-intensive profile is an implicit institution type, not a hard blocker.

surfaceForm: SSSD, realmd, AD/LDAP, OIDC, Apple Platform SSO, Jamf Connect, Entra ID, Conditional Access, Hello for Business, osquery, Jamf, Mosyle, Kandji, Intune, Defender for Endpoint, WireGuard, OpenVPN, Always-On VPN, SSE, Ansible, Puppet, Salt, GitOps, Munki, Apple Business Manager, GPO, auditd, journald, syslog, Windows Event Forwarding, EDR (endpoint integration matrix cells)
proposedGenericDecision: These are generic third-party/OSS/commercial products, NOT UL-specific institutional choices, and the table caption already says 'Each cell is indicative; specific institutional deployments vary.' They are illustrative capability examples, so they do not bind the document to UL. Keep.
rationale: Per the task scope, these are product names, not institution-specific (no UL/uni.lu/RESTENA/etc.). The matrix is explicitly indicative. Recorded as keep so they are not mistaken for institutional bindings during generalization.

surfaceForm: does not engage the specifics of any jurisdiction's procurement law. Institutions verify the language with their own legal counsel.
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch02-conceptual-frame-EN.tex | Sec 2.5 Out of scope (Procurement law bullet)
proposedGenericDecision: Already explicitly jurisdiction-agnostic ('any jurisdiction', 'their own legal counsel'). This is the correct generic posture; keep as an exemplar of how national-transposition assumptions should be handled.
rationale: This passage deliberately avoids naming a country and defers to local counsel - it is the model institution-agnostic treatment, with no implicit national-transposition leak.

surfaceForm: The institutional registry that holds TAC declarations records who validated, who activated, who suspended, who decommissioned ... per the institutional retention schedule / per retention policy
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch02-conceptual-frame-EN.tex | Sec 2.4 Lifecycle (\paragraph{Governance over transitions.}, lifecycle table Decommissioned/Archived rows)
proposedGenericDecision: 'institutional registry' and 'institutional retention schedule/policy' are role-based abstractions, not UL artefacts. No named system. Keep.
rationale: Role-based; refers to a generic registry and retention policy the institution maintains, without naming a UL system, a country retention law, or a governance body. No blocker.

surfaceForm: governance approval recorded ... institutional review (data classification confirmed, policy envelope reviewed, governance approval recorded)
proposedGenericDecision: Refers to a generic 'governance approval' / 'institutional review' without naming a rectorate, board of governors, or DCS-style body. Keep; it is already role-based.
rationale: No named governing body or UL committee; the review/approval step is described by function only. Recorded as a deliberate keep to confirm the lifecycle does not assume a specific governance shape.

surfaceForm: engaged by the institution's existing DR framework ... the institution's HR governance ... an institutional learning-and-development function ... useful in any institution's existing governance ecosystem, not to displace that ecosystem
location: ul-it-policy/technical/ch02-conceptual-frame-EN.tex | Sec 2.5 Out of scope (HR, training, DR bullets and closing paragraph)
proposedGenericDecision: All references are to the receiving institution's own pre-existing functions (HR, L&D, DR), explicitly framed as 'any institution's'. This is the desired generic posture; keep.
rationale: The out-of-scope section is explicitly written to be institution-agnostic ('any institution's existing governance ecosystem'). No UL, no jurisdiction, no named department. Model passage; keep.
